concise_source_summary: Section 6 constructs risk-adjusted dealer positions and customer flows using DV01 and implied volatility. Within-dealer in-sample maxima proxy capacity; capacity weights aggregate normalized utilization. Section 7 models conditional illiquidity quantiles. Appendix A motivates dynamic quoting with state-dependent inventory constraints, expected future capacity multipliers, and a holding-cost extension. These are distinct from forecasting a public signed nominal aggregate’s future absolute sampled peak.
current_claim_judgment: Current Sections 1 and 9 appropriately motivate inventory monitoring while requiring additional contractual and balance-sheet inputs for margin or funding decisions. This source supplies neither the present peak target nor its missing operational cost mapping or an independent same-target baseline.
current_intro_exact: Dealers absorb customer order imbalances while managing inventory risk and scarce balance-sheet capacity. Inventory affects optimal dealer pricing (Ho and Stoll, 1981), FX dealing (Lyons, 1995), and observed inventory adjustment in dealership markets (Hansch, Naik and Viswanathan, 1998). Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.
